title: Advanced HTTP Server Concepts knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Advanced HTTP Server Concepts?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Validate method, path, content type, body size, and input; set appropriate status codes and close resources safely.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Validate method, path, content type, body size, and input; set appropriate status codes and close resources safely.
questions.explanation: Validate method, path, content type, body size, and input; set appropriate status codes and close resources safely. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Advanced HTTP Server Concepts?
questions.explanation: “HTTPS servers” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Advanced HTTP Server Concepts implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
